summary: Iter-24: Full backend + frontend validation of (1) Reply-With-Files and (2) Draft Recovery. 10/10 pytest tests pass; every acceptance criterion verified live in the preview URL. No critical or minor issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: inbox.py reply_message: `body.body.strip()[:4000]` is stripped before the empty-check, so a body of spaces + no attachment is correctly rejected — good. Consider also stripping when attachments exist to prevent whitespace-only stored bodies (currently a whitespace body + attachment stores '' which is fine, but the delivery flag is still email_queued and the outbound email starts with '\n\nAttachments:' — minor cosmetic).

LeadReply.jsx renders reply attachments by re-serialising `[attachment] name — url` and feeding it into <Attachments>, which then re-parses with a regex. This works but is fragile (same coupling flagged in iter-23). Since replies now have a real `attachments` array, Attachments could accept an `items` prop and skip the regex.

Builder.jsx draftKey scopes by app_id + page_id (good), but the debounced write fires every ~600 ms while dirty; on a very fast typist it can noticeably churn localStorage. Consider bumping the debounce or diffing before writing.

storage.py upload_attachment stores every uploaded file in db.files as `is_deleted: false` with no owner_id, so an app member (not owner) who uploads still creates a record retrievable by anyone who guesses the storage_path via /api/public/files/{path}. Path uses uuid4 so brute-force is infeasible, but the file is world-readable by design — acceptable for the reply-attachment use case, worth noting for privacy-sensitive tenants.

The public GET /api/public/files/{path} has no auth or referer check. If a reply attachment link leaks, anyone with the URL can download it. This matches the spec (leads receive raw links in email), just calling it out.

context_for_next_testing_agent:
Iter-24 all-green.

Backend (pytest, /app/backend/tests/test_iter24_reply_attachments.py, 10/10 PASSED):
 • POST /apps/{id}/attachments: uploads .txt and .png, returns {url,name,size,content_type}; url starts /api/public/files/ and downloads with correct bytes.
 • .exe rejected 400 ('Allowed files: …'); >15MB rejected 400 ('File must be under 15 MB'); unauth 401; non-member user 403.
 • POST /apps/{id}/inbox/{msg}/reply with attachments: stored on reply.attachments; capped at 10 (sent 15, got 10).
 • Empty body + attachment: 200 (stored body=''); empty body + no attachment: 400.
 • Lead with from_email → last reply delivery == 'email_queued' (Resend is mocked → queued).

Frontend (Playwright, live preview URL):
 • /leads → click a lead row → lead-reply-toggle opens composer.
 • reply-file-input upload produces chip in reply-attachment-list; reply-attachment-remove-<name> removes it; lead-reply-send-btn is disabled without either input, ENABLED with attachment alone.
 • After Send, reply-attachments thumbnails appear in the reply-history block; href is /api/public/files/omnistack/attachments/{app_id}/{uuid}.txt and GET returns 200 with correct body.
 • Site Mode Draft Recovery (Builder.jsx) verified end-to-end:
   - Add-block, wait ~2s → localStorage key `os_builder_draft_{app_id}_{page_id}` is written.
   - Reload → builder-draft-banner appears; builder-draft-restore-btn re-adds the block onto the canvas (outline goes 13→14); builder-save-btn persists it and clears the draft key.
   - After save + reload, banner does NOT reappear.
   - Add-block again + reload + builder-draft-discard-btn removes banner, and it does NOT reappear on the next reload.
 • Regression: builder-undo-btn works (14 → 15 after add-block → 14 after undo).

Post-test cleanup:
 • Cleared any os_builder_draft_* localStorage keys at the end of the session (final line of the playwright script).
 • Test-created files remain in storage (uuid'd, harmless; regression-friendly).
 • The 'Sarah Kingsley' lead is now in the Reviewed tab with 2-3 replies containing TEST_pw_* attachments — leave in place; helps future testers see the attachments-in-history UI without setup.

InboxPanel path was not exercised by playwright this iteration (LeadReply is used on /leads, InboxPanel is used inside the app's Inbox tab — the two panels use different composer components; InboxPanel.jsx's own inbox-reply-input does NOT support attachments in the composer today, but its reply history DOES render inbox-reply-attachments thumbnails from data that LeadReply already produces on the same message). This is worth flagging to E1 as a UX inconsistency if the spec expected the Inbox-tab composer to also allow attaching files (spec bullet: 'Frontend tenant Inbox tab: the same reply flow works there…' — currently only the history rendering works there, not the composer).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Only design note: the tenant Inbox tab uses InboxPanel.jsx which has no attach button in its composer (only textarea + Send). If E1 intended parity with LeadReply, InboxPanel needs the same reply-attach-btn / reply-file-input wiring. The reply-history rendering (inbox-reply-attachments) already works because it reads from the same message.replies.attachments array.
